title: List colouring
description: List assignments from which a graph cannot be properly coloured: they refute choosability, which is Pi-2-complete once lists of size 3 occur (Erdos, Rubin and Taylor; Gutner and Tarsi). The abstraction guesses the lists, the check finds a colouring from them, and the refinement says that one node loses the colour it was given. The default is K(3,3) with lists of size 2, an easy case; try a = 2, b = 4, p = 4 (144 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The graph, the palette and the list sizes. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% The palette, and size(V,K): the list of node V has K colours.
% (Mix sizes 2 and 3 for the hard case, for example: size(1,3). size(V,2) :- node(V), V > 1.)
colour(1..p).
size(V,2) :- node(V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a list of colours for every node.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a list of the required size for every node.
K { list(V,C) : colour(C) } K :- size(V,K).
#show list/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a proper colouring from the lists (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a proper colouring that gives every node a colour from its list.
1 { col(V,C) : list(V,C) } 1 :- node(V).
:- edge(U,V), col(U,C), col(V,C).
#show col/2.

% The colouring works for all lists that still contain the colours it uses.
relevant(list(V,C)) :- col(V,C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

library.summary: List assignments from which a graph cannot be properly coloured, refuting choosability (K(3,3), lists of 2 out of 3 colours, 36 solutions).

instances.facts:
% The complete bipartite graph with a nodes on the left and b nodes on the right.
left(1..a).
right(a+1..a+b).
node(V) :- left(V).
node(V) :- right(V).
edge(U,V) :- left(U), right(V).
